exposure: Intra-Articular (IA) Tranexamic Acid (TXA) with pericapsular infiltration (0.5 mL adrenaline, 0.4 mL morphine, 1 g vancomycin, 1 mL ketorolac, 15 mL ropivacaine)
Periarticular (PA) Tranexamic Acid (TXA) with pericapsular infiltration (0.5 mL adrenaline, 0.4 mL morphine, 1 g vancomycin, 1 mL ketorolac, 15 mL ropivacaine)
outcome: Blood loss (postoperative haemoglobin levels, haematocrit drop)
Immediate postoperative pain relief (visual analogue scale scores)
Functional outcomes (flexion angles, gait distance, length of hospitalisation stay)
cohort: 63 patients who underwent unilateral primary total knee arthroplasty (TKA).
finding: Both intra-articular and periarticular tranexamic acid combined with analgesic components were equally effective in reducing blood loss and improving immediate postoperative pain relief and functional outcomes.
followup_time: Up to hospital discharge (including Postoperative Day 1 and 2 observations)
